en: The Dharani Divine Spell Scripture of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara with a Thousand Eyes and a Thousand Arms, Volume One.
Translated by the Śramaṇa Zhìtōng of Zǒngchí Monastery during the Great Táng Dynasty.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara addressed the Buddha,
saying, "World-Honored One,
this is due to the inconceivable causes and conditions of my own past merit and virtue."
Now that I have received this prophecy from the World-Honored One,
I wish to benefit all sentient beings by giving rise to great compassion and being able to sever all fetters.
It can extinguish all fears;
all sentient beings who receive this majestic spiritual power shall entirely be freed from the causes of suffering.
They shall obtain the fruit of peace and happiness.
If there are sons or daughters of good family who,
during the five hundred years following my parinirvāṇa, [uphold this teaching].
Those who are able to receive and uphold this dharani mantra gate according to the Dharma during the six periods of day and night will have all their karmic obstructions completely extinguished.
All dhāraṇī and divine mantra dharma-gates shall be fully accomplished.
Now, in order to repay the kindness and virtue of the World-Honored One,
wherever I may be— be it in a village, city, kingdom, town, or settlement— [I shall propagate this].
Whether they be in the mountains and wilds or in the forest groves,
I shall always follow and protect such persons,
ensuring that no ghosts or spirits may harass or harm them.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One."
In the final five hundred years, among sentient beings,
those with heavy defilements and meager merit will be many;
they will be unable to maintain focused mindfulness.
Should there be any who receive [this],
they may be harmed by ghosts or spirits;
now, by the power of the Buddha’s majestic spiritual authority, [I protect them].
Extensively benefiting all sentient beings and bringing peace and happiness to devas, humans, asuras, and others,
he expounded for them the dharma of dhāraṇī.
Throughout immeasurable kalpas in the past,
I have personally approached and made offerings to such dhāraṇī teachings,
as well as to all Buddhas of the past, future, and present.
All have attained *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* by means of this dharma-gate of the dhāraṇī.
If there are good sons or good daughters, etc., who...
For one who single-mindedly recollects and upholds this dharani-dharmaparyāya,
that person in the present life will speak with fluency,
without any obstruction, and their wisdom and eloquence will be thoroughly penetrating.
Among all the great assemblies of devas and humans, they are the most supreme;
those who hear this rejoice and all prostrate themselves before them.
In whatever place they are born, they shall always behold the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṃgha.
That all people believe and accept whatever I say should be known as the majestic spiritual power of all Buddhas,
and not my own power.
At that time, the World-Honored One praised Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, saying:
"Excellent, excellent! You are able to thus benefit and bring peace and happiness to devas, humans, asuras, and others, and to purify the path of karma."
"I now seal this with the Seal of Wisdom,
so that you shall never again fall back.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara—
Again, he addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One,
I recall that within immeasurable kalpas of the past..."
While upholding this dharani-dharma-gate on Mount Potalaka,
he encountered the Mara King leading a host of maras.
They will disturb my Dharma so that the mantras do not succeed.
At that time, I shall use this dharani-method to subdue these māras,
causing them all to retreat and disperse.
One should know that the power of this dhāraṇī is inconceivable.
At that time, out of compassion, for the sake of benefiting others, and for the sake of bringing peace and happiness to devas and humans, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara—
Then he spoke the Dharma of the Mūla-dhāraṇī.
1. The Great Body Dhāraṇī: The First Application of the Universal Encompassing Body Seal of the Thousand-Eyed, Thousand-Armed Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva.
*Namo sarvathāryāya* (Namo Sarva-jñāya). *Namo ratnatrayāya*. *Namo amitābhāya*.
1. *Namo bhagavate*, 2. *tathāgatāya*, 3. *arhate*, 4. *samyaksaṃbuddhāya*, 5. *namo āryāvalokiteśvarāya*, 6.
*bodhisattvāya*, 7. *mahāsattvāya*, 8. *mahākāruṇikāya*, 9. *namo mahāsāhasrapramardanāya*, 10. *bodhisattvāya*, 11. *mahāsattvāya*.
12. Namaḥ mahākāruṇikāya vaṅgāya | 13. Namo vipulavimale | 14.
Supratiṣṭhite | 15. Saṃkṣepa-sūrya-śatasahasrātitejase | 16. Prabhāvabhasita-sitāya svāhā ||
Mūrdhāte (17) mahāmaṇi-makuṭa-cūḍāla-te (18) bhagavati dīrgha-padma-prabhe (19) ye sarva-loka-ā-kāra-pada-ye (20) śamane ca-ye (21). [Note:

Vajravetāliye (45) Lankṛtaśīle (46) Amitābhasya (47) Kāmalalantike (48) Pravarānara nara nariñanamā.
This dhāraṇī is called "The Blessed One’s Adorned Precious Staff of Lotus-Hand.
The World-Honored One spoke it in the Great Vajra Joyful Palace,
where it was praised by the Bodhisattva Uṣṇīṣavijayā and immeasurable devas, nāgas, and kiṃnaras.
In order to shatter the vast mountain of karmic obstructions,
if there are those who hear this dhāraṇī, or read it, or recite it—
All afflictions and karmic obstructions of that person shall be completely eliminated.
If anyone, at the time of dawn, generates a mind of reverence and recites this dhāraṇī, [their merits shall be likewise increased].
Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva will constantly follow and protect this person,
so that all matters they contemplate shall be accomplished.
If there is one who seeks to have their aspirations fulfilled,
they should sit alone in a quiet place,
contemplating Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva in their mind without any other distractions.
If one recites this dhāraṇī seven times, there is no wish that will not be fulfilled.
Furthermore, one will be loved and cherished by all sentient beings and shall not fall into any of the evil realms.
Whether sitting, walking, or standing,
if one constantly brings the Buddha to mind as if he were present before one's eyes,
such a person, throughout immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of births, will [attain...]
All accumulated evil deeds and karmic offenses shall be completely extinguished.
This person shall attain the merit of a thousand-turning wheel-turning kings.
In every birth, they shall always be accompanied by Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva.
Furthermore, if one is born into a noble family and scatters a full handful of fragrant flowers before Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva while reciting this dhāraṇī seven times, [the following shall occur].
One attains the dharma-nature of great compassion and the merit of the great trichiliocosm;
such a person achieves great power in the world.
If one gazes upon the face of a Bodhisattva while reciting this dhāraṇī mantra, [the same shall occur].
One immediately beholds the smiling countenance of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva;
having seen it, one immediately attains the Ground Free from Defilement (vimalā-bhūmi) and is able to illuminate the world.
In this very life, one shall behold the Buddha, who will regard one with compassion and provide guidance;
at the time of death, one will enter as if into meditative absorption;
and in every place of rebirth, one shall attain the knowledge of past lives.
All karmic obstacles and hindrances will be completely extinguished.
If one wishes to receive and uphold this dhāraṇī,
one should do so on the fifteenth day of the waxing moon.
Having observed the eight precepts and donned pure white robes,
one may perform this practice either at a stūpa containing the Buddha’s relics or before an image of the Buddha that contains his relics.

Use white sandalwood to make a paste for coating the altar; grind the white sandalwood on a stone to obtain the powder and use it to smear the ground. Scatter various kinds of flowers within that altar.
Burn incense and light lamps before the Buddha.
One should immediately give rise to a mind of reverence before the Buddha.
Then Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva will enter this maṇḍala;
one should then recite this dhāraṇī one hundred and eight times.
All the karmic obstructions and the grave offenses of the five heinous crimes committed by this person shall be completely extinguished;
their actions of body, speech, and mind will all attain purity.
Having attained the power of the Buddha’s samādhi and the power of empowerment,
they fully accomplish the power of the stages of the pāramitās and the power of supreme wisdom.
When it is time for rain to fall...
If one recites this dhāraṇī while gazing at the heavens,
sweet rain will fall in accordance with the seasons.
If one recites this dhāraṇī while gazing at the earth, [the same shall occur].
It can cause the hundred grains to all reach full maturity.
If one recites this dhāraṇī by the side of a dried-up pond, river,
or spring, [the same result shall follow].
Immediately the water will return and fill it to the brim.
If one suffers from any illness whatsoever,
one should recite this dhāraṇī.
By stroking it with the hand, one will immediately be cured.
Recite this dhāraṇī in the presence of one who has lost mindfulness.
One shall regain right mindfulness.
If one is among those who are hungry or thirsty,
one should look upon their faces and recite this dhāraṇī.
All hunger and thirst will be completely extinguished.
If one wishes to establish a boundary,
one should enter the water of a pool.
If this dhāraṇī is written and fastened atop a banner,
within a range of one hundred yojanas there shall be no misfortunes or afflictions;
it will immediately constitute a consecrated boundary (*sīmābandha*), providing protection and accomplishment.
1. The General Body-Seal of Thousand-Eyed and Thousand-Armed Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, Number One. First, stand upright with the body straight and the feet together.
The right foot is slightly bent;
first, extend the left hand downward and bend the middle and ring fingers together, placing them against the palm.
Extend the little finger, index finger, and thumb,
with the palms facing upward;
then do the same with the right hand.
Bend the elbows so that they align with the shoulders and the navel;
the palms face forward.
This is the mudrā for gathering the body in its entirety.
If one wishes to subdue the hosts of Māra and all externalists with their dense forests of false views, and cause them to enter the right path,
one should form this mudrā and recite the dhāraṇī twenty-one times.
It shall surely be as you wish.
The mantra is:

*Namo ratnatrayāya | namo āryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya mahākāruṇikāya | tadyathā | abate abate | bale bate | hī hī hī | svāhā*. The second Dhāraṇī-mudrā of the Totality for the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara with a Thousand Eyes and a Thousand Arms is identical to the aforementioned body-mudrā.
Place the palms together at the heart;
interlace the five fingers with the left hand pressing over the right,
and extend the two index fingers straight upward with their tips touching.
The thumb is placed alongside the index finger,
pressing down upon the first phalanx;
the palm is slightly opened.
This mudrā is called the Dharma of the Dhāraṇī of Total Retention.
One who performs this mudrā can extinguish and eliminate the evil karma accumulated throughout immeasurable kalpas of birth and death.
Their karmic obstacles will be extinguished all at once;
they shall be reborn in the pure lands of the ten directions in the future.
This was formerly [taught by] the Tathāgata Śākyamuni.
As he was about to attain enlightenment, he was disturbed by the Māra King.
By performing this dhāraṇī-seal of the *dhāraṇī*, he attained the bliss of meditative concentration (*dhyāna-samādhi*).
The mantra is as follows:

*Tadyathā:* (1) *Sarvadhāraṇī* (2) *maṇḍalāya* (3) *khe khe* (4) *pramodita* (5) *sattvāya* (6) *svāhā*. 3. The Mudrā of Liberation and Meditative Concentration (*vimokṣa-dhyāna-mudrā*). This is the third mudrā of the Thousand-Eyed and Thousand-Armed Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva. First, bare the right shoulder, place the right knee on the ground, and join the palms above the crown of the head.
Bend the two index fingers so that their tips touch one another;
place the two thumbs upon the second phalanges of the index fingers.
This mudrā method is named the Mudrā of Liberation from Meditative Concentration (*vimokṣa-dhyāna-samādhi-mudrā*).
The Buddhas of the past all cultivated this Dharma together,
thereby attaining meditative concentration, liberation, and supernormal powers;
they constantly made offerings with this very Dharma.
One shall see all the Buddhas of the ten directions as clearly as if they were right before one's eyes.
[Recite] the same mantra as before. 4.
The Thousand-Eyed Seal Mantra of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara with a Thousand Eyes and a Thousand Arms. The Fourth: The Thousand-Eyed Seal Mantra. Stand up with both feet together.
First, with the middle, ring, and little fingers of both hands,
place the backs of the nails against one another.
Then, extend the two index fingers upright so that their tips touch.
Place the side of the right thumb against the upper joint of the second phalanx of the index finger;
with the wrists separated by about five inches, position them between the eyebrows.
This is called the Thousand-Eyed Mudrā (*Sahasranetra-mudrā*).
One who practices this dharma-gate of mudrās and mantras will immediately behold hundreds of thousands of myriads of koṭis of Buddha-fields and pure, wondrous lands;
in each and every Buddha-land, one shall encounter one million four thousand bodhisattvas.
One must be a companion to the practitioner;
if one has not yet passed through the three maṇḍalas,
one shall certainly not be able to see this dharma-gate of seal-mantras.
This dharma-seal causes one to eliminate transgressions; it has been personally verified by Bodhisattvas as a method for receiving the Dharma and wisdom.

Whatever aspirations one may have shall all be fulfilled. The mantra is: Oṃ sarvacakragarāya dhāraṇī indriye svāhā. The Fifth: The Universal-Gathering Seal of the Thousand-Armed Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva. Stand upright with feet together.
First, turn the right palm upward with the five fingers each touching one another;
then, with the left palm...
Press the right palm upward against the chest;
this is called the Seal of the Universal Gathering of the Thousand Arms.
This seal is able to subdue the demonic adversaries of the trichiliocosm.
The mantra is:

*Tadyathā* (1) *parogiti* (2) *sarvavārāya* (3) *sarvaduṣṭa* (4) *ugramaye* (5) *svāhā* (6). This is the Seal for Accomplishing the Samādhi of Universal Penetration (*Sampūrṇa-samādhi-mudrā*). It is the sixth seal of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara of a Thousand Eyes and a Thousand Arms. To perform it: stand up and place the heels together.
First, with the left hand, extend the five fingers and clasp them together, then bend the elbow and thrust it forward.
Next, do the same with the right hand,
bending the elbow and thrusting it inward.
This is called the Samādhi Seal of Penetration.
This seal enables one to penetrate all seals of wisdom regarding samādhi,
and adorns the eighty-four thousand dharma-gates through skillful means.
All have attained *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* by means of this dharma.
Using the aforementioned Great Body Mantra (Mahākāya-dhāraṇī): 7.

The Seal for Summoning the Assembly of Devas, Nāgas, and the Eight Classes of Spirits and Ghosts of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva with a Thousand Eyes and a Thousand Arms. Seventh: Stand up with both feet together.
First, with the ring finger of the left hand,
press upon the nail of the thumb;
next, do the same with the right hand.
The two little fingers and the middle fingers are held upright with their tips touching;
the wrists are joined and pressed together.
Move the index fingers back and forth.
The mantra is:

Oṃ sarvadevanāgā ānaya svāhā. This is the eighth seal for summoning Mahābrahmā and Kauśika to inquire about the Dharma, belonging to the Thousand-Eyed and Thousand-Armed Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva; it follows the previous seal.
Open the wrists and support them with the sides of the hands.
With the palms facing upward, move the index fingers back and forth.
The mantra says:
Oṃ mahābrahmaya hī hī svāhā. This seal and mantra method can gather together all the immeasurable and innumerable dharanī and seal dharma-gates so that they all assemble here.
If, during a solar or lunar eclipse,
one recites the mantra over clarified butter twenty-one times and seals the butter with the mudrā before consuming it, [the practitioner will attain the desired results].
This seal-dharma gate makes people intelligent and enables them to recite ten thousand verses daily.
It was bestowed by the Tathāgata Sūryagarbha upon the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.
9. The Seal of the Joyful Maṇi Wish-Fulfilling Bright Jewel of the Thousand-Eyed and Thousand-Armed Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva. Ninth: Standing upright with palms joined at the heart.
Bend both thumbs inward into the palms,
extend the remaining four fingers straight upward, and join the palms at the heart;
recite the aforementioned Great Body Mantra twenty-one times.
One will certainly attain entry into the palaces of the various devas and travel through the Buddha-lands of the ten directions;
hundreds of thousands of millions of precious jewels shall be available as required at will.
They shall all attain the opportunity to make offerings to all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, Vajras, and the entire assembly of holy ones.
If there is anyone capable of performing this dharma-gate,
they should rise early in the morning and perform purification by washing and rinsing their mouth.
By performing this mudrā rite,
one beholds the Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges in the ten directions,
and eradicates the heavy sins of birth and death accumulated over immeasurable kalpas.
Therefore, one praises such merits. 10.
The Prayer According to One’s Heart Seal of the Thousand-Eyed, Thousand-Armed Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva: The Tenth Prayer According to One’s Heart Seal follows the previous seal.
Bend the two middle fingers and press them against the backs of the two thumbs,
with the tips of the nails touching each other.
Use the preceding mantra.
If a person fulfills all their sought-after vows, they will certainly never retreat from the path to Bodhi. 11.
The Seal of the Samādhi of Entering the Extinction-Samādhi of the Thousand-Eyed and Thousand-Armed Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, Number Eleven. This follows the previous seal.
Straighten and spread the fingers, with the thumbs extended;
open the palms.
This mudrā is that which I employed when I was on the stage of the causal ground.
Thereupon, Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges received this Dharma from me,
enabling me to realize the path of Bodhi.
I then recited the Great Body Dhāraṇī.
12. The Seal for Requesting the Buddha’s Samādhi of the Thousand-Eyed and Thousand-Armed Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, the Twelfth. As before, join the palms at the heart.
Moving the index finger back and forth, the mantra is recited:

Oṃ sarvabuddhasamaya khe he he pramuditāsattva svāhā. Regarding the method for establishing the ten-cubit maṇḍala altar of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva with a thousand eyes and a thousand arms: next, the ritual for the altar is explained.
Whenever performing any maṇḍala ritual, according to the careful consultation of the Sanskrit original,
it is stated that in this land there is no ground suitable for constructing a maṇḍala.
Just as in India, they all select the most excellent and meritorious sites to establish their ritual enclosures (*maṇḍala*).
In the land of the Brahmins, there are specific methods for selecting such sites,
which cannot be explained in detail here.
Furthermore, let us discuss this foremost mountain dwelling in this land of China, a place of leisure and tranquility.
At the summit of the mountain, there is a site with favorable geomantic features;
one should excavate the earth there, removing stones, pebbles, shards, and other types of foul soil.
Then, having leveled and smoothed the ground,
he smeared it with fragrant *gomaya* mixed with incense,
measuring sixteen feet in length and breadth.
The foundation should be twelve or even sixteen finger-breadths high;
one cubit is considered the most excellent.
First, one should take white sandalwood incense.
Grind [the substance] upon that stone,
take the powder and smear it over the maṇḍala,
and delineate the boundaries using five-colored powders.
The altar has four gates opened.
At the eastern gate is installed the Heavenly King Dhṛtarāṣṭra;
at the southern gate is installed the Heavenly King Virūḍhaka.
The Heavenly King Virūpākṣa is stationed at the western gate;
the Heavenly King Vaiśravaṇa is stationed at the northern gate.
In this manner, the heavenly kings are installed in succession.
The attendants and their retinues each occupy their respective positions.
In the center of the maṇḍala,
place an image of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara with a Thousand Eyes and a Thousand Arms.
Arrange an altar before [the image].
Upon the altar, place the dhāraṇī rites,
burn various kinds of incense, and set out various kinds of food and drink.
They scattered various kinds of flowers as offerings,
with the sole exception of miscellaneous items, pungent herbs, wine, and meat; apart from these,
they prepared fresh fragrances, flowers, trees, fruits, and other such things anew every day.
Before the image, one should offer the three white foods—milk, curd, and ghee—and honey;
burn sandalwood, aloeswood, ghee-blended incense, and camphor incense;
and bathe at the three times of day while receiving the threefold vows.
Recite the mantra with a sincere heart to make offerings to the Thousand-Eyed Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva.
Make these offerings at dawn, at noon, and at dusk,
ensuring they are not omitted on any given day.
In this manner, continuing for up to twenty-one days,
once the offerings have been completed with full devotion, he comes to see the mantra-master,
who performs the ritual behind a consecrated altar (*maṇḍala*).
It is stated that all [deities] are summoned and depicted in painted images;
however, consulting the Sanskrit original, there is no such matter.
It merely indicates that the mantra-practitioner faces the east while reciting the mantra.
Perform the first, second, third, and so on up to the twelfth [mudrās].
Regarding the Samādhi Seal for Inviting the Buddha, what need is there to laboriously establish a separate seal?
Perform each of the preceding seals once and recite the mantra seven times for each.
Up until the completion of the twelfth mudrā,
one should personally resolve upon non-retrogression with firm steadfastness;
merely by performing the rite of invocation, all will come.
Cause them to resolve upon the mind of bodhicitta.
Sitting upright, visualize all the mantra deities before you;
there shall be no obstacles whatsoever, and they will not fail to reach the ultimate goal.
Recite the aforementioned Great Body Mantra one thousand and eighty times.
At that time, Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva shall manifest and take on the physical appearance of Ānanda.
When he came to inquire, "What dharma do you require as a practitioner? What vow do you seek? this was personally asked by Zhìtōng (Jītong) during his offerings, and thus it is recorded here.
The practitioner replied, "I seek the dhāraṇī dharma for the sake of unsurpassed bodhi."
When you receive the prediction of enlightenment,
I only wish that you would give rise to a sincere and earnest mind, seeking neither fame nor profit,
and that your aspiration be to rescue all sentient beings, regarding them as one's only child.
Furthermore, may all ghosts and spirits submit in accordance with this vow.
Once the wish is fulfilled, one should know it only within oneself;
it must not be proclaimed to others.
According to the general translation, this method is identical to that of Xuánmú; Xuánmú received this teaching and stated:
"If one wishes to seek the fulfillment of all vows, one should perform the four-cubit water maṇḍala rite."
Burn aloeswood incense and recite the preceding mantra one hundred and eight times.
Form the tenth "Petition for Wishes" mudrā as before;
then all wishes will be fulfilled according to one's desires.
Immediately burn this single copy.
Beyond this, there is no other such offering;
all dharani dharma-gates will be fully accomplished.
Furthermore, if one wishes to cause all to be joyful,
one should perform the aforementioned ninth seal of the Wish-Fulfilling Mani Jewel and recite the body-mantra.
One should recite the mantra twenty-one times over sesame seeds and burn them in the fire.
One will immediately obtain one's wish.
If one desires to cause Kharaja to rejoice,
one should take a branch from a tree within the Kharaja garden.
Recite the mantra twenty-one times and cast it into the garden;
they will immediately become joyful.
If one wishes to subjugate wicked people or enemies:
One should recite the mantra over twenty-one pieces of *kaṭuka* wood and burn them in the fire;
they will immediately submit and be subdued.
Furthermore, if there are spirits or ghosts who are difficult to subdue, [the following method should be employed].
Take guggulu incense and white mustard seeds;
recite the mantra twenty-one times over them and cast them into the fire to burn.
All spirits, ghosts, and those afflicted by illness will naturally submit as subjects.
It is recorded that when an epidemic spreads,
one should construct a water maṇḍala four cubits in size.
Take high-quality cow’s ghee, recite the mantra over it one hundred and eight times, and burn it in a fire.
All pestilences and epidemics will be completely extinguished.
Furthermore, if one takes a small portion of ghee and gives it to a person afflicted by an epidemic to eat, they will be cured immediately.
In the past, an epidemic spread throughout the kingdom of Kaśmīra.
Those who contracted the illness died within no more than one or two days.
There was a Brahmin named Zhendi (Candraprabha) who brought this dharma-practice [to that land].
Epidemics shall be extinguished immediately at their proper time;
when the king of pestilence spirits departs from the borders of the kingdom, one will know that the efficacy [of the rite] has been realized.
Furthermore, there is a method for when other nations invade and surround [the realm], or when bandits and rebellions arise.
If one performs the aforementioned first General Body-Seal Mantra one hundred and eight times,
all thieves and robbers will naturally be extinguished.
